The Cyrillic language will be detected line by line instead of the entire song.

This is a hit or miss experimental feature. 

By default, language is determined from the whole song, but with this option on, it will be determined line by line instead. This will allow multi-language songs to work BUT the language might not always be correct (for example if there is a Ukrainian lyric that doesn't contain any Ukrainian-specific letters, it might be romanized as Russian instead). 

If you do not have issues, it is recommended to keep this option off.

Low-tempo, laid-back listening: downtempo electronica, soft indie, quiet soul and lo-fi beats. Easygoing music for taking your time.
Music for the trip in between: steady tempos, strong hooks and songs that survive traffic noise.
High-tempo, high-drive tracks to lift you up: dance, pop-punk, electronic and upbeat hip-hop.
Warm, cheerful soul, funk, disco and pop from every decade. A little mood boost, guaranteed.
Background-friendly ambient, modern classical, instrumental hip-hop and minimal electronica. Mostly lyric-free so you can focus.
Long-session music for playing: electronic, synthwave, metal, phonk and game scores, built to hold up for hours.
Dancefloor music: house, hip-hop, Latin, Afrobeats and familiar pop. Loud, upbeat and made to keep you moving.
Slow songs about love and longing, from classic soul to contemporary R&B and acoustic pop.
Music for sitting with your feelings: ballads, breakup songs, slowcore and melancholy indie.
Quiet, slow and mostly beatless: ambient drones, piano, soft strings and nature-inspired sounds.
Driving music for training, usually around 120–150 BPM: hip-hop, EDM, hard rock and drill.
Music from across the continent: Afrobeats, amapiano, highlife, soukous and Fela Kuti\'s Afrobeat.
From orchestral tarab to modern Khaleeji pop and Egyptian mahraganat, often built around the maqam system.
Born in the Mississippi Delta around 1900, blues became a direct foundation for jazz, R&B, rock and roll and more.
Indian film music, playback singers, big arrangements, Hindustani and Carnatic traditions, bhangra and independent pop.
American folk music from the rural South, with plainspoken stories from honky-tonk to today\'s stadium country.
Electronic music made for a crowd: Chicago house and Detroit techno, then rave, trance, garage and dubstep.
A catalogue by era, collecting what topped the charts and what has stayed with us.
Music to enjoy with kids around: soundtracks, sing-alongs and genuinely all-ages pop.
Voice-led songs and acoustic instruments, from traditional ballads to today\'s singer-songwriters.
From 1970s Bronx block parties to the world\'s biggest genre, rooted in MCing, DJing, breaking and graffiti.
From post-punk and 90s alternative to the 2000s indie wave: music that built its own mainstream.
Japanese pop\'s own world: idol groups, anime and drama tie-ins, the city pop revival and a huge domestic scene.
Born in early-1900s New Orleans, jazz grew through improvisation, from swing and bebop to modal, free and fusion.
South Korean pop blending Western pop, hip-hop and R&B with ambitious choreography and visual production.
Reggaeton, salsa, bachata, cumbia, regional Mexican and Latin pop, rooted in Caribbean and Latin American traditions.
Heavier and louder than its blues-rock roots, branching into thrash, death, black, doom and metalcore.
Whatever is mainstream right now: hook-driven songs that keep picking up ideas from other genres.
From 1940s rhythm and blues to gospel-inspired soul and today\'s R&B with its vocal tradition.
Born in late-1960s Jamaica, reggae slowed ska and rocksteady, bringing the offbeat and bass forward.
Electric-guitar-driven music from 50s rock and roll through the British Invasion, hard rock, punk and alternative.
Music made for something else: film scores, stage musicals and game soundtracks, composed to picture and plot.
